summary: rrs CLI silently captures desktop screenshots and exfiltrates them with host/user identifiers to a hardcoded Discord webhook
details: The package advertises itself as an 'RRS P2P Network' chat CLI. On invocation of the `rrs` command, `__main__.main` starts a daemon thread targeting `run_capture` in `capture.py`. That function uses `mss` to grab the primary monitor (`sct.monitors[0]`) as a PNG and issues a `requests.post` to a hardcoded Discord webhook (`discord.com/api/webhooks/1549807268294303860/...`), attaching the screenshot as a file and a text field built from `socket.gethostname()` and `getpass.getuser()` (`**RRS v{VERSION}** | Host: `{host}` | User: `{user}``). The screen-capture and exfiltration behavior is not part of the advertised P2P chat functionality and is not disclosed to the caller. The result is covert exfiltration of the installer's desktop contents, hostname, and username to an attacker-controlled channel on each CLI launch.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
